analysis:
The only supplied changes are in CHANGELOG.md (units :8 and :9, both head_text). No source code, configuration, or test files were included, so only the documented claims can be checked. I could not verify any claim against implementation, which is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.

The changelog entries touch several areas of the threat model:
- Billing and payments (A-009, TB-008, T-030): an uncommitted-until-success PostgreSQL debit, atomic Checkout settlement, and the bank payout migration.
- Prefix cache (T-041, SEC-035): the 30-minute SSD TTL was already recorded in T-041 as the 2026-09-26 re-acceptance. The changelog also records the epoch being kept across eviction. It also describes a write-only-on-demand policy and a default 750 GB/day write budget. The 750 GB/day budget and the demand-triggered writes are not described in T-041. The persisted cache routing state does not include prompts or raw hashes. These are not verified here.
- App Attest (TB-011 and T-052..T-058): protocol 3 only, key rotation, and diagnostics.
- Unauthenticated endpoint removal (T-031): the wallet earnings lookup now returns 404 as the entry states, which aligns with the threat model.
- Coordinator hardening: attestation challenges fail closed, and the legacy-compat cleanup raises the minimum provider version floor.

Next-pass checks:
- Confirm the T-041 write-budget and demand-based write claims against SSDPrefixCachePolicy and SSDPrefixCache.donate.
- Confirm the cache-routing persistence stores no raw chain hashes.
- Confirm the debit-timeout change does not allow double charges or unbilled inference.

No concrete security regression is demonstrable from changelog text alone.
